May climatologically brings Manila's peak temperatures averaging 33–34°C, with minimal precipitation before the monsoon onset. eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects high uncertainty in forecast models for São Paulo's highest temperature on May 11, with implied probabilities tightly clustered at 37.5% for 20°C, 37.0% for 18°C, and 36.0% for 21°C, driven by an advancing cold front from the South. INMET's May 4-11 weekly outlook indicates mostly stable weather in the Southeast with low cloudiness and possible weak showers in southern São Paulo, but the front's timing could introduce southerly winds, increased cloud cover, and rain that suppress peak daytime heating below May climatological averages of 22-23°C. Model ensembles diverge on frontal passage speed—earlier arrival favors 18-19°C maxima via cooler air advection, while delays allow 20-21°C—pending tomorrow's updated INMET and CPTEC guidance. Urban heat island effects at official stations like Mirante de Santana add minor variability to observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in forecast models for the highest temperature at Lagos' Murtala Muhammed International Airport on May 11, with GFS and ECMWF runs clustering implied highs around 32–33°C amid the seasonal shift from dry harmattan to early monsoon influences. Recent airport observations show daily peaks of 32–33°C over May 7–9, buoyed by NiMet's 2026 seasonal prediction of prolonged dry spells through May that limit convective cooling despite rising humidity and isolated thunderstorms. Key differentiators include potential afternoon cloud cover suppressing peaks below 32°C or clearer skies pushing toward 34–35°C under emerging El Niño-neutral conditions favoring heat; daily NiMet updates and model refreshes will clarify steering patterns and storm risks before resolution.
